title: Control whittler notes — SOC2 prep scratchpad
content:
Quick brain-dump / scratchpad for mapping controls to practical evidence. Intent: make a minimal set of artifacts we can assemble for the auditor, while keeping this lightweight and defensible. Not a finished checklist — more a working map and open questions log.

Context: small team ramping for SOC2 Type 1 readiness on hosted + private offerings. We need concrete picks for evidence (logs, configs, runbooks, PRs) and a plan to fill gaps. Focus areas below reflect recurring auditor asks: access control, change management, logging/monitoring, incident response, vendor management, and data segregation for Private deployments.

---
Top-level mapping ideas (rough)

- User access / identity (CC6/CC7):
  - Evidence: Okta groups export (export date stamped), role-to-permission matrix for Console and API, examples of inactive accounts removal runbook.
  - Controls to highlight: MFA enforcement on console and service accounts, least privilege roles in RBAC, SSO SCIM provisioning configuration.
  - Quick doc names: okta-groups-export-2026-02.csv, rbac-role-matrix-v1.md, svc-account-deprovision-checklist.md

- Key management & encryption (CC6):
  - Evidence: KMS key policy snapshots, rotation schedule, HSM integration notes for private deploy, code reference where keys are referenced (config samples), encrypted volumes evidence for dedicated nodes.
  - Concern: in private deployments customers may manage keys — need clear boundary statement for auditor.

- Change control / release process (CC3):
  - Evidence: PRs that show reviews for runtime changes, release notes, canary rollout config in console, rollback playbook entries.
  - Candidate artifacts: github PR 1987 (runtime kernel tweak), release-note-2026-01-24.md, rollout-policy-canary.md

- Logging / monitoring / retention (CC4):
  - Evidence: Log retention policy doc, sample of token-level cost/latency dashboard export, alerting rule exports (PagerDuty or internal on-call rotations), example of trace for a failed request and postmortem.
  - Note: need to confirm retention durations for hosted logs vs. private (customers may set retention).

- Incident response & DR (CC5):
  - Evidence: incident runbook (owner/contact table), recent postmortem (redacted), tabletop exercise notes, SLA incident handling procedure.
  - Action: find one postmortem with full timeline we can include (redaction ok).

- Vendor & subcontractor controls (CC2):
  - Evidence: vendor inventory, risk assessment matrix, SOC2/ISO certs from major cloud provider, signed DPA templates.

- Data isolation / segregation (Dedicated & Private):
  - Evidence: network diagrams for Private deploy, VPC peering docs, signed architecture diagram for Dedicated capacity, examples of access logs showing tenant isolation.
  - Open: we need a short declarative paragraph explaining how routing / smart routing respects tenant isolation at the control-plane level.

---
Evidence inventory (sketch) — single-line artifact name => where/how to produce it

- okta-groups-export-2026-02.csv => Okta admin console export (Arjun)
- rbac-role-matrix-v1.md => docs repo / trust-ops (Noelle)
- kms-policy-snapshot-02-2026.txt => KMS console / Terraform state export (Marta)
- pr-1987-runtime-kernel-tweak.md => Github PR + review thread link
- rollout-policy-canary.md => product-console repo / playbooks
- logs-sample-latency-export-2026-02.csv => observability exports (Grafana/Console)
- incident-2026-01-highlatency-pm-redacted.pdf => internal postmortem export (redact user IPs)
- vendor-inventory-2026.tsv => trust-ops spreadsheet (shared)
- private-network-diagram-v3.png => architecture repo (svg export)

---
Open questions / decisions to surface

1) Private deployments & KMS boundary: auditors will expect clarity on who controls keys. We need a short statement for each private deployment option (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed). Is there a standard one-liner legal has approved? (Ask: legal@)

2) Logging retention values: hosted default = 365d? Need authoritative confirmation from observability team; what about trace/kv cache telemetry?

3) Evidence of automated deprovision: Do we have a runnable job that deactivates employees after LDAP deactivation, or is it manual? If manual, we need compensating evidence and a short improvement plan.

4) PR sampling strategy: auditors typically want several examples across infra, runtime, and console. Which PRs best represent change control (one infra, one runtime, one console)? We have PR 1987 for runtime; need infra + console picks.

5) Role of Dedicated vs Hosted in SLA language: need a single paragraph explaining how we measure latency SLOs for Dedicated customers (is it 99th p50/p95? where documented?).

---
Short-term action list (owners + ETA)

- Assemble RBAC / Okta export + map to roles (Noelle) — ETA 2026-03-05
- Pull KMS policy snapshots & note rotation cadence (Marta) — ETA 2026-03-04
- Export 3 PRs for change-control evidence (Arjun) — ETA 2026-03-06
- Draft KMS boundary wording for private deployments + ask Legal (Noelle -> Legal) — ETA 2026-03-09
- Get confirmation on log retention from observability (Ping: #observability-team) (Marta) — ETA 2026-03-03

---
Notes to self / misc fragments

- Keep one redacted postmortem with timeline; auditors like an incident that shows end-to-end detection/response. Avoid including IPs or user PII.
- Consider a small script or single-run demo that shows Okta -> SCIM removal -> downstream deactivation to strengthen evidence. Could be recorded video + logs.
- When assembling artifacts, include a short README.txt per artifact explaining why it’s relevant and the extraction method (auditors like reproducibility).
- Slack threads to capture: #trust-ops incident-2026-01 (link), #platform-release for PR approvals.

Unresolved bits: legal tag for KMS boundary, definitive retention numbers, one infra PR pick.

End of scratchpad — will convert to a tidy checklist once artifacts exist.

-- Noelle
